title: RT by @rob_svrn: Nick Bostrom argues humans may be as incapable of imagining AI’s upside as apes are of imagining human life: "It looks like there's a gradient in the world in terms of AI sentiment, where the US is kind of on the negative extreme of that. People in China, for example, are much more excited about this." "A large chunk of the potential upside is more of the way of unlocking new ways to be human, new possible modes of being." "Imagine some great ape ancestors of Homo sapiens deliberating whether they should continue to evolve and one day become human. They would realize some of the benefits, like, 'We could have unlimited bananas.' And that's true." "But it would miss out on most of what's good about being human. Great literature and art and humor and politics and spirituality." "It would be presumptuous for us to think that now we have achieved the level of enlightenment where all possible values are transparent to us. Think of a big cathedral of possible modes of being. We have basically explored the janitor's closet."

name: Rob Greer
title: RT by @rob_svrn: Every time something scarce became abundant, the world changed so fast that the people living through it mistook the beginning for the end. Food was scarce for a hundred thousand years. Agriculture made it abundant, and people who had spent every waking hour chasing their next meal suddenly had something they had never owned before. Time. That time became villages. The villages became cities. The cities became language carved into clay, and then law. Nobody standing in a wheat field understood they were building Rome. Information was scarce for millennia. The printing press made it abundant. The church lost its monopoly on knowledge, and within two centuries every throne in Europe was shaking. Nobody pulling letters from a press understood they were ending the divine right of kings. Energy was scarce until we learned to crack the earth open. Coal and oil made it abundant, and a single person could suddenly command the force of a thousand. Within one generation the entire structure of work turned inside out. Nobody shoveling coal understood they were building the middle class. The pattern never changes. A resource that was hoarded becomes available. The people who held it resist. The structures built on that scarcity fall. And whatever rises in their place is invisible from where everyone is standing. Here is the part almost everyone misses. Information stopped being scarce a long time ago. The library, the search engine, the endless feed. We have been drowning in information for decades, and it never set anyone free, because information just sits there. It answers only the question you already knew how to ask. Intelligence was the thing still locked away. A mind on the other side. Something that explains, argues back, catches your mistake, and meets you exactly where you are standing. The part that bends toward you instead of forcing you to bend toward it. That is what broke open. For the first time, a person with nothing but curiosity and a connection can reach an intelligence that teaches, challenges, and builds alongside them in real time. No tuition. No admissions office. No permission. The distance between what a person can imagine and what they can actually make is collapsing in front of us. And the people most threatened by that are not the ones without talent. They are the ones whose entire standing depends on talent staying rare. Every credential, every hierarchy, every quiet system that decided who was allowed to build and who was told to watch, is resting on a foundation dissolving underneath it. They will fight it. They always do. The church fought the press. The aristocracy fought the vote. The owners fought the union. Every single time a scarce thing became abundant, the ones who controlled it warned everyone else that the sky was falling. The sky was never falling. The ceiling was lifting. And the people underneath it, the ones who had been told their whole lives that the ceiling was the sky, finally looked up and saw nothing there to stop them. That is what is happening right now. Intelligence was never rare. Access to it was. Access just became free. Whatever gets built in the next ten years will not come from the rooms we are all watching. It will come from someone who was never supposed to have the tools, who right now has no idea that the thing they are doing has a name, or a scale, or a future. Same as the wheat field. Same as the press. Same as the coal. We never recognize Rome while we are still building it.

name: Rob Greer
title: RT by @rob_svrn: $TAO is still very much correlated with the rest of crypto, not AI. And I think that is going to change in 2027. Right now, the price of TAO is still largely driven by the same forces that move the rest of the crypto market. Bitcoin goes up, TAO follows. Bitcoin goes down, TAO follows. Meanwhile, the actual Bittensor ecosystem is developing at a pace that is increasingly disconnected from its market valuation. But something important is happening underneath the surface, and I believe it will fundamentally change how TAO is valued. The ecosystem is starting to generate meaningful revenue from outside of crypto, and more importantly, an increasing number of subnets are using that revenue to buy back and burn their Alpha tokens. This is where Bittensor is different compared to the rest of crypto. Because Alpha tokens are connected to TAO through their liquidity pools, demand for Alpha also creates demand for TAO. Every subnet that builds a successful business and uses (part of) its revenue for buybacks contributes to this mechanism. And the beauty of it is that this doesn't depend on attracting new crypto investors or convincing people to buy TAO because of hype and narrative like 99% of crypto. It depends on businesses and consumers paying for products they need in the real world. This is what I mean when I say Bittensor will start growing from the inside out. The ecosystem increasingly develops its own internal source of demand, funded by real economic activity. And we don't need all subnets to succeed for this to become significant. A handful of breakout subnets generating tens or even hundreds of millions in annual revenue could already make create significant demand. Now imagine what happens when that number keeps growing. That's why I expect 2027 to be the year we see a meaningful repricing of $TAO. Enough thoughts for this morning, enjoy your saturday. Oh and let me know what you think.
